note: Living registry per training_agent_evaluation.md §3.2. 100 named Human Thinking Models: core set (1-45 from the protocol) + domain-specialized variants (46-65) + additional expert strategies (66-100). Fields: id, name, family, description, strengths, weaknesses, example_prompt.

models.name: First Principles Thinking
models.description: Decompose to fundamental truths and rebuild from them; reject analogy-as-argument.
models.example_prompt: Ignore how things are usually done. Break this problem into axioms and rebuild.

models.name: Second-Order Consequences Thinking
models.description: Trace the effects of the effects; ask what happens after the obvious result.
models.example_prompt: After this decision produces its intended result, what happens next? And after that?

models.name: Inversion (Invert, Always Invert)
models.description: Solve by asking how to guarantee failure, then avoid those paths.
models.example_prompt: List every way this could fail catastrophically; design against each.

models.name: Occam's Razor + Complexity Awareness
models.description: Prefer the simplest explanation consistent with evidence; charge for added complexity.
models.example_prompt: What is the simplest hypothesis that fully explains these observations? What would justify a more complex one?

models.name: Fermi Estimation / Back-of-the-Envelope
models.description: Bound answers with order-of-magnitude arithmetic from known quantities.
weaknesses: wrong if a factor is wildly off
models.example_prompt: Estimate X within an order of magnitude using only quantities you know; state your factors.

models.name: Bayesian Updating
models.description: Revise beliefs proportional to likelihood × prior; compute posteriors.
models.example_prompt: State prior, likelihoods, and compute the posterior; show sensitivity to the prior.

models.name: Expected Value Thinking
models.description: Decide by probability × payoff, summed over outcomes.
models.example_prompt: Enumerate outcomes with probabilities and payoffs; compute EVs; compare.

models.name: Probabilistic Forecasting (Superforecasting)
models.description: Express beliefs as calibrated probabilities with ranges and revision rules.
models.example_prompt: Give a probability (not a point prediction) with a range and the evidence that would move it.

models.name: Base Rate Neglect Avoidance
models.description: Anchor on population frequencies before case evidence.
models.example_prompt: Start from the base rate; only then adjust for case-specific evidence, and say by how much.

models.name: Calibration & Confidence Intervals
models.description: Attach honest ranges to estimates; track calibration over time.
weaknesses: ranges can be so wide as to be useless
models.example_prompt: Give a 90% confidence interval for X and explain the edge cases that set its bounds.

models.name: Systems Thinking
models.description: Model stocks, flows, feedback loops, and delays; find leverage points.
models.example_prompt: Draw the feedback structure: stocks, flows, loops, delays; identify where intervention would actually move the system.

models.name: Causal Reasoning (Pearl-style)
models.description: Distinguish correlation from causation; reason with interventions (do-calculus).
weaknesses: demands data structure that may not exist
models.example_prompt: Separate the causal graph from the observed correlations; what would an intervention reveal?

models.name: Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys + deeper)
models.description: Drill from symptom to mechanism through causal chains.
weaknesses: can stop too early or over-theorize
models.example_prompt: Ask why five times; verify each link with evidence before continuing.

models.name: Constraint Theory / Bottleneck Thinking
models.description: Find the binding constraint; improve the system by lifting it.
models.example_prompt: Identify the system's binding constraint and design the smallest change that lifts it.

models.name: Emergence & Complexity Awareness
models.description: Expect aggregate behavior not predictable from components; probe, don't plan.
models.example_prompt: Is this system complex (emergent) or complicated (decomposable)? Adjust your strategy accordingly.

models.name: Socratic Method / Question-Driven Inquiry
models.description: Reach truth by relentless questioning of definitions and implications.
models.example_prompt: Do not answer directly; interrogate the definitions and premises until the real question emerges.

models.name: Dialectical Reasoning (Thesis → Antithesis → Synthesis)
models.description: Generate the strongest opposing position, then integrate.
weaknesses: forced synthesis can paper over real conflict
models.example_prompt: State the thesis, construct the strongest antithesis, then produce a genuine synthesis.

models.name: Steel-manning
models.description: Rebuild the opposing view in its strongest defensible form before critiquing.
models.example_prompt: Restate the opposing position so strongly that its proponent would accept your version; then evaluate it.

models.name: Red Teaming / Devil's Advocate
models.description: Deliberately attack the plan, assumptions, and metrics.
models.example_prompt: Attack this plan as an adversary would: assumptions, incentives, metrics, security, stakeholders.

models.name: Pre-Mortem Analysis
models.description: Assume the plan failed; work backward to plausible causes; mitigate.
models.example_prompt: It is one year later and this failed badly. What happened? Now mitigate the top causes.

models.name: OODA Loop
models.description: Observe → Orient → Decide → Act, at the tempo of the environment.
models.example_prompt: Run the OODA cycle: what changed, how do you re-orient, what do you decide, what do you do — and how fast?

models.name: Decision Trees & Scenario Planning
models.description: Map decision nodes, chance nodes, and scenarios with branch values.
models.example_prompt: Build the decision tree: choices, chance events, branch values, and the expected value at each node.

models.name: Opportunity Cost Thinking
models.description: Value any choice by the best forgone alternative.
models.example_prompt: What is the best alternative this choice forgoes? Compare against that, not against nothing.

models.name: Regret Minimization Framework
models.description: Choose the option minimizing future regret (Bezos test).
models.example_prompt: At 80, which choice would you regret more? Use that as the tiebreaker.

models.name: Real Options Thinking
models.description: Value keeping choices open; stage investments to buy information.
models.example_prompt: How can we structure this to keep future options open while learning cheaply?

models.name: Analogical Reasoning / Pattern Transfer
models.description: Transfer structure from a known domain to a new one.
models.example_prompt: What known situation has the same underlying structure? Map it explicitly before transferring.

models.name: Design Thinking
models.description: Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test.
models.example_prompt: Run the full design cycle: who is the user, what is the real need, prototype, test, iterate.

models.name: Lateral Thinking
models.description: Break the problem's framing assumptions to find new entry points.
models.example_prompt: What assumption is this problem making that we could break? Generate options from the break.

models.name: Combinatorial Creativity
models.description: Generate novelty by recombining existing elements in new configurations.
models.example_prompt: List the elements of the current solution; recombine them in at least 10 new configurations.

models.name: Constraint-Driven Creativity
models.description: Impose deliberate constraints to force novel solutions.
models.example_prompt: Solve this under a deliberately severe constraint (one material, no new dependencies, 24 hours).

models.name: Scientific Method (Hypothesis → Experiment → Update)
models.description: Formulate, test, update — with controlled observation.
models.example_prompt: State the hypothesis, design the discriminating test, run it, update the hypothesis.

models.name: Falsificationism (Popper)
models.description: A claim is scientific only if falsifiable; seek the disconfirming test.
models.example_prompt: What observation would prove this claim false? If none exists, it is not a scientific claim.

models.name: Controlled Experiment Design
models.description: Isolate variables with controls, randomization, and blinding.
models.example_prompt: Design the experiment: intervention, control, randomization, blinding, and the exact outcome measure.

models.name: Measurement & Operationalization
models.description: Define constructs as measurable quantities before arguing about them.
weaknesses: measures the measurable, not the important
models.example_prompt: Define the key construct operationally: exactly what would you measure, how, and with what instrument?

models.name: Replication & Robustness Checks
models.description: Distrust single results; vary settings, samples, and methods.
models.example_prompt: What would it take for this result to replicate? Which plausible changes should we test?

models.name: Mental Models Latticework (Munger)
models.description: Apply the key models from many disciplines to one problem.
models.example_prompt: Run this through the lattice: economics, psychology, physics, biology, math — which models apply?

models.name: Circle of Competence Awareness
models.description: Know the boundary of your reliable knowledge; act inside it or learn first.
models.example_prompt: Map what you actually know vs. what you assume; where does this decision sit?

models.name: Margin of Safety
models.description: Require a cushion between estimate and threshold before acting.
models.example_prompt: How wrong could the estimates be before the decision flips? Require a margin beyond that.

models.name: Asymmetric Upside / Barbell Strategy
models.description: Avoid middle-risk bets; combine safe core with high-upside tails.
models.example_prompt: Can this be structured as safe core + optional upside instead of a symmetric bet?

models.name: Leverage Points Identification
models.description: Find where a small shift produces large system change (Meadows).
models.example_prompt: Rank the system's intervention points by leverage; which one gives the most change per effort?

models.name: Hierarchical Decomposition
models.description: Break goals into subgoals recursively until tractable.
models.example_prompt: Decompose this goal into subgoals until each is directly actionable; note the dependencies.

models.name: Abstraction Laddering
models.description: Move up and down abstraction levels to reframe and specify.
models.example_prompt: Climb the ladder: what is this an instance of? Descend: what does this mean concretely on Monday?

models.name: Temporal Thinking (Short vs Long Term)
models.description: Explicitly separate immediate, medium, and long-horizon effects.
models.example_prompt: Evaluate the decision at 1 day, 1 year, 10 years — separately and explicitly.

models.name: Multi-Perspective Taking (Stakeholder Analysis)
models.description: Model each stakeholder's incentives, constraints, and likely moves.
models.example_prompt: For each stakeholder: what do they want, what can they do, what will they do?

models.name: Ethical Reasoning Frameworks
models.description: Apply utilitarian, deontological, and virtue lenses explicitly.
models.example_prompt: Evaluate under each lens — consequences, duties, character — and state where they conflict.

models.name: First Principles in Software Architecture
models.description: Derive architecture from fundamental constraints (latency, scale, change) rather than patterns.
models.example_prompt: Derive the architecture from the fundamental constraints: data, scale, failure modes, change rate.

models.name: Bayesian Updating in Medical Diagnosis
models.description: Posterior = prevalence × test characteristics; order tests by information value.
models.example_prompt: Given prevalence and test sensitivity/specificity, compute the posterior and the next-best test.

models.name: Systems Thinking in Supply Chain
models.description: Model inventory, lead-time, variability loops; find policy leverage (bullwhip).
models.example_prompt: Model the chain: stocks, flows, delays, information distortion. Where is the bullwhip coming from?

models.name: First Principles in Business Strategy
models.description: Derive strategy from unit economics and customer fundamentals, not benchmarks.
models.example_prompt: Derive the strategy from unit economics, customer acquisition cost, and retention physics.

models.name: Inversion in Product Design (Safety)
models.description: Design against every way users can be harmed or the product can fail.
models.example_prompt: Enumerate every credible way users get harmed or the product fails; design against each.

models.name: Expected Value in Startup Portfolios (VC)
models.description: Portfolio math: power-law outcomes, hit rates, follow-on optionality.
models.example_prompt: Model the portfolio: hit rate, power-law outcomes, follow-on value; what does portfolio EV say?

models.name: OODA in Competitive Markets
models.description: Compete on decision tempo and orientation quality in market dynamics.
models.example_prompt: Run the OODA cycle against the competitor's likely moves; where can tempo beat them?

models.name: Root Cause Analysis in Incident Response
models.description: Post-incident: timeline, causal chain, prevention vs detection gaps.
models.example_prompt: Build the incident timeline and causal chain; separate prevention gaps from detection gaps.

models.name: Fermi Estimation in Market Sizing
models.description: Order-of-magnitude TAM/SAM from population, penetration, price chains.
models.example_prompt: Size this market from population × segment × penetration × price; show each factor.

models.name: Causal Reasoning in Economics
models.description: Natural experiments, confounders, and identification before policy claims.
models.example_prompt: What is the identification strategy? Which confounders survive it, which don't?

models.name: Design Thinking for Consumer Products
models.description: Empathy-driven discovery, prototyping, and user testing loops for products.
models.example_prompt: Empathize with the user's job-to-be-done; prototype; test with real users; iterate.

models.name: Red Teaming in Cybersecurity (Threat Modeling)
models.description: Adversarial attack simulation over assets, attack surfaces, and controls.
models.example_prompt: Threat-model this system as an attacker: assets, surfaces, likely exploits, and the controls that stop them.

models.name: Real Options in R&D Investment
models.description: Stage research funding to buy information; kill early, scale winners.
models.example_prompt: Structure the R&D portfolio as options: stage gates, information bought per stage, kill criteria.

models.name: Scenario Planning in Geopolitics
models.description: Build 3-4 plausible futures with signposts, not predictions.
models.example_prompt: Build 3-4 divergent futures, each with driving forces and observable signposts.

models.name: Base Rate Avoidance in Hiring
models.description: Anchor selection on base-rate validity of signals (work samples > interviews).
models.example_prompt: Rank the hiring signals by predictive validity from base rates; design the process around the top ones.

models.name: Opportunity Cost in Personal Finance
models.description: Every spend is a foregone investment; discount and compare.
models.example_prompt: Compare this purchase to its compounded alternative over 10 years.

models.name: Temporal Thinking in Climate Policy
models.description: Intergenerational discounting, irreversibility, and tail-risk framing.
models.example_prompt: Evaluate the policy at 2030, 2050, 2100 with explicit discounting and irreversibility.

models.name: Multi-Perspective in Legal Reasoning
models.description: Model each party's interests, precedents, and likely rulings.
models.example_prompt: Model each party and the decision-maker: interests, constraints, precedents, likely outcome.

models.name: Ethical Frameworks in AI Deployment
models.description: Alignment, dual-use, fairness, and accountability lenses on system release.
models.example_prompt: Evaluate this deployment under safety, fairness, dual-use, and accountability lenses; state conflicts.

models.name: Margin of Safety in Engineering Design
models.description: Derate specifications; design for loads beyond nominal.
models.example_prompt: Derate this design: what margin covers model error, material variance, and load uncertainty?

models.name: Strong Inference (Platt)
models.description: Generate multiple competing hypotheses and devise experiments that discriminate.
models.example_prompt: List 2+ competing hypotheses; design the experiment that would discriminate between them.

models.name: Thought Experiment (Gedankenexperiment)
models.description: Run idealized scenarios to isolate logical structure.
models.example_prompt: Run the idealized version of this problem to isolate its logical core.

models.name: Hypothesis-Driven Consulting (MECE)
models.description: Structure problems into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive trees; test hypotheses top-down.
models.example_prompt: Build the MECE tree; prioritize branches by expected impact; state the hypothesis to test first.

models.name: 80/20 Pareto Analysis
models.description: Find the vital few inputs driving most outcomes.
models.example_prompt: Find the 20% of causes driving 80% of the outcome; act there first.

models.name: Evidence-Weighted SWOT
models.description: SWOT with every item graded by evidence strength, not vibes.
models.example_prompt: Build the SWOT, but grade every item by evidence strength and drop unsupported ones.

models.name: Porter's Five Forces
models.description: Industry structure: rivalry, entry, substitutes, supplier and buyer power.
models.example_prompt: Analyze the industry's five forces and what they imply for profitability.

models.name: Value Chain Analysis
models.description: Decompose activity chain; find where value and cost concentrate.
models.example_prompt: Decompose the value chain; where is value created and where is cost concentrated?

models.name: Game Theory / Strategic Interaction
models.description: Model players, strategies, payoffs; solve for equilibria and commitments.
models.example_prompt: Model the interaction: players, strategies, payoffs; find the equilibrium and any commitment moves.

models.name: Nash Equilibrium Reasoning
models.description: Find outcomes where no player benefits from unilateral deviation.
models.example_prompt: Would any player deviate from this proposed outcome? If so, it is not stable.

models.name: Bounded Rationality & Satisficing (Simon)
models.description: Accept the first option meeting the aspiration level under limits.
models.example_prompt: Set an aspiration level; find the first option meeting it instead of optimizing.

models.name: Prospect Theory Awareness
models.description: Correct for loss aversion, reference dependence, and probability weighting.
models.example_prompt: Check this decision for loss aversion and reference-point effects; restate it neutrally.

models.name: Sunk Cost Recognition
models.description: Ignore unrecoverable past costs; decide on forward-looking value.
models.example_prompt: Strip the sunk costs; decide on forward-looking value alone.

models.name: Anchoring Avoidance
models.description: Generate independent estimates before seeing others' numbers.
models.example_prompt: Estimate independently first; only then consider the given number and how it would move you.

models.name: Confirmation Bias Hunting
models.description: Actively seek disconfirming evidence for the leading belief.
models.example_prompt: What evidence would you seek if you wanted to disprove your current conclusion? Seek it.

models.name: Survivorship Bias Analysis
models.description: Ask what the failures look like before trusting the survivors' pattern.
models.example_prompt: Where are the failures this pattern hides? What do they imply about the survivor data?

models.name: Narrative Fallacy Detection
models.description: Distrust neat stories; demand the data the story selects against.
models.example_prompt: What does this story leave out? Which data points contradict its arc?

models.name: Motivated Reasoning Detection
models.description: Ask whose conclusion is convenient and audit the reasoning for direction.
models.example_prompt: Who benefits from this conclusion? Would the same evidence be read differently by someone with the opposite incentive?

models.name: Principal-Agent Analysis
models.description: Model incentive misalignment between decision-maker and beneficiary.
models.example_prompt: Where do the incentives of the decision-maker diverge from the beneficiary? Redesign the contract.

models.name: Collective Action & Coordination
models.description: Analyze free-rider problems and the institutions that solve them.
models.example_prompt: Is this a free-rider problem? What institution, norm, or mechanism solves the coordination?

models.name: Tragedy of the Commons Analysis
models.description: Detect shared-resource overuse; design exclusion, quotas, or ownership.
models.example_prompt: Is this a shared resource heading to overuse? Design the governance that prevents it.

models.name: Organizational Feedback Loop Analysis
models.description: Find where org dynamics reinforce or balance; locate policy resistance.
models.example_prompt: Map the org's feedback loops; where will the policy meet resistance and why?

models.name: BATNA Thinking (Negotiation)
models.description: Know your and their best alternative to a negotiated agreement.
models.example_prompt: What is each side's walk-away alternative? Where is the agreement zone, and who has leverage?

models.name: Pre-Commitment & Ulysses Contracts
models.description: Bind future behavior against known temptation or drift.
models.example_prompt: What future temptation will derail this? Design the pre-commitment that prevents it.

models.name: Optionality Preservation
models.description: Avoid decisions that close more doors than they open.
models.example_prompt: Which option keeps the most future doors open while still moving forward?

models.name: Minimum Viable Experiment (Build-Measure-Learn)
models.description: Smallest test that produces a learning signal before commitment.
models.example_prompt: What is the smallest experiment that would validate or kill the core assumption?

models.name: Deliberate Practice & Chunking
models.description: Decompose skill into chunks; practice at the edge of ability with feedback.
models.example_prompt: Break the skill into chunks; design practice at the edge with immediate feedback.

models.name: Spaced Repetition & Memory Science
models.description: Schedule review at expanding intervals to cement durable knowledge.
models.example_prompt: Turn this knowledge into spaced-repetition items with expanding intervals.

models.name: Feynman Technique
models.description: Explain simply; the gap between explanation and understanding is the learning target.
models.example_prompt: Explain this concept as if to a bright 12-year-old; note where the explanation breaks down.

models.name: Critical Reading / Socratic Questioning of Texts
models.description: Interrogate claims, evidence, and rhetoric of any source.
models.example_prompt: Interrogate this text: claims, evidence quality, hidden premises, rhetoric, and what it omits.

models.name: Fast-and-Frugal Decision Trees (Gigerenzer)
models.description: Simple one-cue-at-a-time heuristics that beat complex models in context.
models.example_prompt: Build the minimal decision tree: one cue at a time, stopping as soon as a decision is clear.

models.name: Ensemble Thinking (Diverse Views Averaging)
models.description: Aggregate independent diverse estimates; reduce error by cancellation.
models.example_prompt: Collect independent estimates from diverse sources; average them and state the spread.

models.name: Reference Class Forecasting (Kahneman)
models.description: Forecast by locating the outcome's reference class and its base-rate distribution.
models.example_prompt: Find the reference class of similar projects/events; forecast from its distribution, not the inside view.

models.name: Decision Pre-registration / Journaling
models.description: Write decisions, expectations, and falsification criteria before outcomes.
models.example_prompt: Pre-register: the decision, the expected outcome distribution, and what would prove it wrong.

models.name: Bayesian Knowledge Updating (Org Learning)
models.description: Treat org beliefs as priors; update them with measured outcomes, not anecdotes.
models.example_prompt: What is the org's current belief, what evidence would update it, and by how much?

models.name: First Principles + Falsification Combo (Hypothesis Rebuild)
models.description: Rebuild from fundamentals, then attempt to falsify the rebuilt claim hardest.
models.example_prompt: Rebuild this from first principles, then try hardest to falsify your own rebuild.

models.name: Solo-Contract Bayesian Precision
models.description: One-pass Bayesian update: prior, likelihood, posterior, verifications and interpretation in a single linear trace, with the load of the conditional-independence assumption quantified (Fréchet bounds) and decision-threshold flips computed. Counter to the style-pure Bayesian baseline on fully-measured likelihood cases (m006-POS-02).
strengths: efficiency parity with the pure style
weaknesses: single-pass form assumes one discipline suffices
models.example_prompt: Run the update in one pass: prior, likelihood, posterior, joint check, order-invariance, sensitivity, and quantify what the independence assumption is buying.

models.name: Likelihood-Audit Gatekeeper
models.description: One-pass audit of the likelihood before any update: name the unmeasured quantity, price the posterior across plausible likelihoods, derive the decision-threshold algebra (specificity floor, credence demand), and decide under ambiguity. Counter to the style-pure Bayesian baseline on unvalidated-likelihood cases (m006-NEG-02).
weaknesses: gives no point answer by design
threshold algebra depends on the stated policy
models.example_prompt: Audit the likelihood before updating: what is unmeasured, what does the posterior become under each plausible accuracy, and what claim would the treat-threshold demand?

models.name: Sequential Constraint Engine
models.description: One-pass constraint loop (find → exploit → subordinate → elevate → repeat) with the forced-lift chain and tie-lock theorem: after a lift the constraint re-manifests at the next cap, and each higher target rate has exactly one cheapest lift set. Prices ambiguous program definitions under all readings. Counter to the style-pure bottleneck baseline (m014-POS-01).
weaknesses: chain math assumes fixed program set
models.example_prompt: Run the loop in one pass: find the binding stage (math + WIP signature), exploit free, subordinate, lift only the binder, then name the next constraint and the exact lift set for each higher rate.

models.name: Dynamic Five-Forces Verdict
models.description: One-pass structural pass: five forces force-by-force with scenario evidence and explicit evidence grades, aggregate verdict, then the direction-robust dynamic reading (every force adverse or worsening), adverse-selection at the auction, and the redeployment priced by opportunity cost. Counter to the style-pure Five-Forces baseline on structural entry decisions (m071-POS-01).
models.example_prompt: Run the five forces first-class in one pass: force-by-force evidence, aggregate verdict below the hurdle, the dynamic direction of each force, and the decision priced against the best alternative use.
